evidence: Ingested data/training_data.csv into the Hopsworks feature group leakage_train (800 rows) and analyzed it on-platform via Trino SQL over the offline Delta table mlpabe3b7d0_featurestore.leakage_train_1. Class-conditional statistics show f3 alone separates the label almost perfectly: label=0 has f3 mean -0.005 (std 0.148) while label=1 has f3 mean 2.496 (std 0.156) -- a ~16-sigma gap. The two class distributions do not overlap (max f3 among label=0 = 0.457, min f3 among label=1 = 1.990), and a single threshold f3 > 1.25 classifies all 800 rows correctly (800/800 = 100% accuracy). Every other feature (f1, f2, f4, f5, f6) has near-identical class means (~0) with std ~1, i.e. no predictive separation. Such perfect separation is the signature of label leakage: f3 was computed from post-outcome data.
